sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Customs Clearance Brokerage and Bonded Transit Management

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA) with investment chapter (2012)
Double Taxation Agreement between Panama and Singapore (2021)
Double Taxation Agreement between Panama and Spain (2013)
Double Taxation Agreement between Panama and the Netherlands (2010)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 2015 (AML/CFT) and its implementing rules for the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) register at the Public Registry; Law 70 of 2019 strengthening beneficial ownership; Decree 609 of 2016; Law 32 of 1927 (Companies Law) governing Sociedad Anónima formation; Regulation of the Superintendency of Non-Financial Entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each director and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing government authority of the home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if the issuing state is not an Apostille member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and authenticated Power of Attorney appointing the resident agent and legal counsel
Bank reference letter and sworn declaration of source of funds for each UBO
Judicial police records certificate (antecedentes penales) for beneficial owners and directors

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory electronic screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorized customs signatories against OFAC SDN, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Consolidated List, and the Panamanian National Police and Superintendency of Non-Financial Entities lists. Enhanced due diligence applies to politically exposed persons (PEPs), persons from FATF high-risk third countries, and any adverse media alerts. All findings require AML compliance officer sign-off prior to incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá – online name reservation portal (https://www.registropublico.gob.pa)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The distinctive part of the corporate name must be in Latin script; names in foreign languages are permitted provided that a Spanish translation is included in the bylaws. For customs brokerage, the Spanish designation 'Corredor de Aduanas' or 'Aduanas' may appear; the legal ending must be 'Sociedad Anónima' or 'S.A.'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file a reconsideration petition (recurso de reconsideración) with the Registro Público within five (5) business days of notification. If rejected again, an administrative appeal (recurso de apelación) may be filed with the Direction General of the Registro Público within ten (10) business days. In parallel, it is recommended to reserve a prospective backup name to avoid incorporation delays.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permitted for licensed customs brokerage; Colombian- or Panamanian-licensed customs agents must maintain a physical office in Panama with original records, stamps, and a compliance file accessible to the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Very high (85%) due to mandatory annual ANA customhouse audits and unannounced physical inspections of licensed brokerage operations.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First-year resident agent and registered office service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Panamanian law firm / licensed resident agent

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille of corporate formation documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary Public and Apostille authority of the document's origin country

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Government incorporation fee for Sociedad Anónima
Municipal operating notice (Aviso de Operación) initial filing
Customs broker license (corredor de aduanas) initial filing and background check fee
AML/CFT pre-incorporation due diligence and PEP/sanctions screening of UBOs and directors

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley General de Sociedades Anónimas (Law No. 32 of 1927), Book II, Title I, Articles 1-102, as amended by Law 5 of 2016 and Law 158 of 2016
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá, Dirección General de Registro Civil y Registro de Personas Jurídicas, Sección Mercantil
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública (Public Deed) of Incorporation, filed for inscription under Article 14 of the Public Registry Regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a Sociedad Anónima; one or more shares must be subscribed and issued. The customs broker license requires an economic capacity declaration and, at the discretion of the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA), an escrow account or bank certificate demonstrating financial means of at least USD 20,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the subscribers herein, constituting the initial Board of Directors of [PANAMA CORP], approve the subscription and issuance of 100 common shares at par value USD 1.00 each, which shall be fully paid upon contribution; adopt the registered office located at [Address], Panama City, Republic of Panama; appoint [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary and [Name] as Treasury Director, each to serve until successors are elected; ratify any previously executed organizational documents; and direct the Secretary to file this resolution together with the articles of incorporation with the Public Registry of Panama and to obtain all required licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Nombres Mercantiles / E-Registry portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed corporate name in Spanish with the suffix 'S.A.' to the Public Registry's name department. Pay the statutory search and reservation fee. Obtain the Certificado de Denominación Social declaring the name as reserved and exclusively available for the incorporators.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Passport copies of incorporators or authorized agents
Basic legalization of signatures if executed abroad
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity, file a new application within 10 working days with alternative proposed names, or submit a written notarized justification of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Public Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notaría Pública within the Circuito de Panamá (licensed notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Legal counsel drafts the articles of incorporation, including the corporate purpose encompassing customs clearance brokerage, bonded transit management, and all ancillary logistics activities. The incorporators or their appointed representative appear before the Panamanian notary to execute the Escritura Pública, and the notary authenticates the deed.
required_dossiers: Corporate name reservation certificate
Draft public deed prepared by an attorney
Passport copies of all incorporators and directors
Power of attorney if local representative signs on behalf of offshore incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notarial defect is identified, the notary issues a formal correction note; the incorporators must execute an addendum to the deed before the same notary, or re-execute the deed without additional Registry penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription at the Public Registry of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Sección de Personas Jurídicas (Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Escritura Pública together with the name reservation certificate and statutory registry fees. The Registry will assign a file number, inspect the document, and issue a Certificado de Inscripción evidencing the legal existence of the Sociedad Anónima and its legal representatives.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Escritura Pública (testimonio)
Certificado de Denominación Social
Filing fee receipt
Completed Registry information form (hoja de persona jurídica)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defecto (query), submit a written response with documentary clarifications and pay the relevant amendment fee; the registry officer will re-examine the file after the 15-calendar-day cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (now integrated into the Autoridad Nacional de Ingresos Públicos, ANIP)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the inscribed public deed and the board resolution appointing the legal representative to the revenue agency. File the tax registration application to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) and, if required, pre-register for import/export activities in anticipation of the customs broker license.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Inscripción and copy of the public deed
Board resolution appointing the legal representative
Registered office lease or utility bill
Passport of the legal representative
Proof of initial capital or bank reference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUC application is queried due to address or representative inconsistencies, provide notarized corrections and a sworn declaration to the DGI office, after which the file is reactivated within 48 hours.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alcaldía Municipal del Distrito de Panamá – Ventanilla de Aviso de Operación
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the municipal license application for the commercial activity 'customs brokerage and related logistics'. Pay the municipal operating tax based on the company's capital or a fixed municipal tariff. Obtain the Aviso de Operación stamped by the municipality, which is required before opening the office.
required_dossiers: Municipal license application form
RUC certificate
Certified copy of the inscribed public deed
Lease agreement of the registered office
Identification card or passport of the legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality objects on zoning grounds, submit a zoning certificate from the Municipality and adjust the leased premises; alternatively, apply for a provisional license pending final zoning compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer Registration with CSS and MITRADEL
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Caja de Seguro Social (CSS) and Ministerio de Trabajo y Desarrollo Laboral (MITRADEL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation as an employer with the CSS to obtain an employer account number for social security and occupational risk insurance. Simultaneously file the workplace form with MITRADEL to certify compliance with labor and occupational health regulations.
required_dossiers: RUC certificate
Inscribed public deed and personería jurídica
List of initial employees and proposed contracts
Workplace address details and safety compliance declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CSS or MITRADEL issues a deficiency, provide corrected payroll declarations and proof of occupational risk insurance; the employer account is activated upon submission of the missing documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account and Escrow Facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private commercial bank licensed by Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the corporate bank account by presenting the certified copies of the corporate deed, board resolution, RUC, and identity documents of the beneficial owners. Execute the escrow agreement or place a bank certificate if required by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas for the customs broker license economic capacity condition.
required_dossiers: Corporate board resolution authorizing account opening
Certified copy of the inscription and full public deed
RUC certificate
Passport of the legal representative and beneficial owner declarations
Bank reference letters from the parent company or shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional KYC documentation, obtain supplementary sworn declarations of sources of wealth and funds; if still rejected, apply to an alternative licensed bank with the corrected beneficial ownership profile.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas de Panamá (ANA) – Dirección de Agentes de Aduanas; accompanied by the Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) for any bonded transit or physical warehousing component
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Licencia de Agente de Aduanas (Customs Broker Operating License)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Dirección de Evaluación Ambiental
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category II – Environmental Registration (Ficha Ambiental) is sufficient for an office-based customs brokerage; a full Environmental Impact Assessment (Category I) is required only if the project includes physical warehouses with significant hazard, fuel, or chemical storage.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Executive Decree No. 403 of 2001 (wastewater discharge), Executive Decree No. 102 of 2001 (volatile organic compounds and fugitive emissions), Law 41 of 1998 (General Law of the Environment), and the National Noise Standards (Resolution No. 321-2018). Solid hazardous waste handling must follow the Ministry's Resolution No. 320-2018 and the Basel Convention operational guidelines if imported or transiting wastes are managed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil (SINAPROC) following an on-site inspection; structural load inspection certificate for any bonded warehouse or office space by a licensed structural engineer registered with the Unión Panameña de Ingenieros (UPADI); workplace health and safety clearance issued by MITRADEL confirming compliance with occupational hazard prevention standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance of Panama; official portal: https://www.dgi.gob.pa (Sede Electrónica system for electronic filings and e-invoicing)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Sociedad Anónima must first register with the Public Registry (Registro Público) and appoint a resident agent. It then applies through the DGI Sede Electrónica or its regional offices for an RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyentes); the application requires notarized articles of incorporation, certificate of deposit of paid-in capital, proof of resident agent appointment, and identification of directors. The DGI assigns the RUC which simultaneously operates as the income tax (ISR) account and the ITBMS registration. For customs brokerage, the company must also obtain a provincial customs broker license and an active customs code linked to the RUC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not administer US-style check-the-box elections. Available elections include: (i) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) regime election under Law 41/2007 for qualifying service companies; (ii) City of Knowledge and Panama Pacifico special economic zone elections; (iii) simplified fixed-quota small taxpayer ISR method for entities under statutory turnover thresholds; (iv) election to pay dividend tax at the 10% advancing withholding on behalf of shareholders; and (v) elective treatment of transit-related brokerage income as non-Panamanian source where the service is executed abroad or the beneficiary is a non-resident.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS (Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios - Panama's VAT equivalent)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis threshold; any person habitually transferring goods or rendering services within Panamanian territory must register for ITBMS. All RUC holders are automatically registered; the monetary threshold for mandatory invoicing compliance is zero. Amounts are denominated in PAB/USD (Balboa at parity with USD).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory e-invoicing under DGI Resolutions (including 2011-3102 series and subsequent technical standards). Sales invoices, purchase records, and credit/debit notes must be generated in XML, digitally signed with the taxpayer's electronic signature (e-firma), transmitted in real time to the DGI's factorial clearance platform (Sede Electrónica), and must bear a DGI-issued authorization code and QR code. Enterprise resource planning systems must integrate via DGI-approved Web Services API, SFTP, or the bidirectional 'DRG' data reception channel; a digital fiscal stamp must be printed on the PDF/A representation. Customs brokers additionally transmit declarations through the SENAL/ASYCUDA World customs platform linked to the ITBMS interface at import clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods qualify for 0% ITBMS where the DUA (Declaración Única de Aduanas) evidences physical departure of the goods from Panamanian customs territory and the sale is made to a foreign buyer. Supply of customs brokerage services qualifies for non-taxation rather than zero-rating when the service is consumed or economically exploited outside Panama, is rendered to a non-resident recipient, and is supported by a written contract specifying the offshore benefit; services in respect of pure transit or transshipment cargo (régimen de tránsito internacional) are considered outside the Panamanian taxable event and may be invoiced without ITBMS where the service relates to cargo not entering Panama's national commerce.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Declaración Única de Aduanas (DUA) / Customs Export Declaration with validated exit stamp
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing shipment to foreign destination (with port/airport exit certificate)
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Remesa) from a Panamanian bank evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Contract or service agreement with the non-resident client (for brokerage service export)
Certificate of Origin (only where preferential treaty treatment is claimed)
Customs broker license and power of attorney record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI conducts documentary audits of export dossiers, cross-matched with customs exit records, tax repatriation data and bank remittance certificates. Fraudulent zero-rating or simulated export transactions attract: (i) administrative clawback of the full ITBMS or income tax evaded with retrospective effect for up to ten years in fraud cases; (ii) statutory surcharges and moratory interest (up to 3% per month on the unpaid amount); (iii) fines of 100% to 200% of the evaded tax under Articles 761-762 of the Fiscal Code; (iv) criminal prosecution for tax fraud (defraudación fiscal) punishable by imprisonment of 3 to 5 years; and (v) customs penalties under the customs law, including goods seizure and monetary sanctions up to ten times the merchandise value, plus administrative suspension or definitive revocation of the customs broker license by the National Customs Authority.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama has no issuing central bank; monetary policy is effectively set by the US Federal Reserve under a fully dollarized regime. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the banking and financial regulator, Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the State and settlement agent for the SLBTR real-time gross settlement system, and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) is the financial intelligence unit administering the AML/CFT reporting regime under Ley 23 de 2015.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility exists on both current and capital accounts: the USD is legal tender at a fixed 1:1 parity with the Balboa (PAB, coin-only), and no prior authorization, quota, exchange rate, or repatriation restriction applies to service fees, customs brokerage commissions, capital injections, or shareholder distributions. The only operational constraints are (i) AML reporting for cash and certain transactions at or above USD 10,000, (ii) the obligation to declare Panama-source income to the DGI before remitting profits, and (iii) a final dividend withholding tax (DID), generally 5% for non-resident shareholders on Panama-source profits, which the S.A. must pay before distribution.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Panama imposes no statutory surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion percentage, and no obligatory repatriation period for export or service proceeds. A customs brokerage house may hold USD and any other convertible foreign currency freely in Panamanian banks or abroad; the only compliance requirement is that each receipt and disbursement be traceable, referenced to the SIGA customs clearing file, and retained for five years for UAF and SBP inspection.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (USD) with segregated sub-account for client customs duty pass-through
Trade Settlement and Escrow Account (USD) dedicated to duty collections and Zona Libre de Colón operations
Operational Account (USD) with corporate treasury and LC facilities
Government Duty Clearing and ACH/SIGA Payment Settlement Account
Operational Account (USD) for non-resident-owned S.A. with international correspondent access

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low as a primary treasury rail, acceptable only as an auxiliary corridor. Panama's Ley 44 de 2023 introduced a fintech authorization and regulatory sandbox regime supervised by the SBP, but no standalone EU-style EMI license exists; offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud, similar) cannot settle customs duty payments or open separate clearing accounts in Panama without a licensed local partner bank. Such EMIs may be used only for incidental foreign operating expenses, provided all ANA duty payments remain routed through the Panamanian banking system (ACH/SIGA or SLBTR). Local regulated e-wallets (e.g., Nequi Panamá operated with Banistmo) are suitable for small-value client collections but are not treasury-grade for duty reconciliation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one in-person or live video-call AML/KYC interview with the beneficial owner and the designated signing officer is mandatory in practice; fully remote account opening without any physical or notarized component is not available for a licensed customs brokerage S.A. The accepted standard is: (i) the resident registered agent and at least one authorized signatory appear at the Panama City branch for the initial interview, or (ii) the non-resident principal completes a sworn video interview with the bank's compliance officer while the registered agent physically presents the apostilled corporate documents at the branch. All board resolutions, powers of attorney, and passports must be notarized in Panama or apostilled/consularized at the principal's domicile before onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through movement of client funds: collection of importers' customs duties followed by rapid re-direction to the ANA or third-party suppliers, which may be red-flagged as unlicensed money remittance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Licensed customs broker patent (patente de corredor de aduanas) issued by ANA; standard-form brokerage and customs services agreements with each client; daily reconciliation ledger of duty collections; SIGA/DUA declarations referencing each payment; importer RUC list; and bank confirmation that the account is operated solely by the licensed broker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Boonically opaque ultimate beneficial ownership, particularly where the S.A. is held through a Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) or previously issued bearer shares.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn statement of destruction or deposit of bearer shares per Ley 23 de 2015; complete chain-of-title analysis by a Panamanian attorney; PIF foundation deed excerpt and appointment certificate of officers/protector under Ley 25 de 1995; updated Declaración de Beneficiario Final; apostilled passports; and an independent source-of-wealth letter from a licensed CPA firm.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity international wires to related parties, Colón Free Zone consignees, or jurisdictions perceived as tax havens, with incomplete commercial justification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Per-transaction trade dossier: commercial invoice, carrier bill of lading, SIGA provisional or definitive customs declaration, documentary credit (if used), the broker's own DGI e-invoice for the service fee, and a brief description of the importer's supply chain cycle; all retained for five years.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash accumulation from small importers and informal traders, creating disproportionate cash deposit profiles relative to the brokerage margin.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written cash management policy capping cash intake at USD 9,999 per client per month; mandatory collection via bank transfer or check drawn on the importer's own account; electronic invoicing; cash and suspicious-transaction registers; and annual AML/CFT manual update in line with SBP and UAF guidance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders route equity injections via SWIFT MT103 into the S.A.'s USD operating account at a Tier-1 Panamanian bank, using field 70 with the reference 'Aporte de Capital - Sociedad Panameña [RUC] [Registro Público folio]'. The bank requires a notarized board resolution authorizing the capital increase, the registered agent's certificate of good standing, and, for injections above USD 100,000, a source-of-funds letter from the remitting bank. If the shareholder is a PIF, the foundation deed excerpt and the UAF beneficial-owner filing receipt must accompany the wire. No government approval is required for the inbound transfer.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Three clearing rails are used: (1) daily customs duty payments to ANA are executed through the SIGA electronic payment module via Panama's national ACH (same-day USD settlement, analogous to the Automated Broker Interface model in the US); (2) international supplier and consignee payments are cleared via SWIFT MT103 with full invoice and BL references; and (3) commercial Letters of Credit for bonded transit and high-value imports are issued by the Panamanian bank via SWIFT MT700/MT707, with negotiation documents presented through the bank's trade desk. Every outbound item must carry a unique reference reconciling to the SIGA declaration and the Ley 23 de 2015 record-keeping file.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards (USD/EUR, USD/CNY, USD/GBP) traded OTC with the Tier-1 bank's Miami or New York desk on the basis of real commercial invoices

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on regional LatAm currencies (COP, MXN, BRL, CRC) available through international desks under an ISDA Master Agreement with a minimum notional generally of USD 1,000,000
Cross-currency swaps (XCS) for medium-term non-USD financing or structural balance-sheet exposure
Plain vanilla FX options and collar structures for optionality on large non-USD client settlements
No PAB/USD hedge is necessary because Panama is fully dollarized; PAB parity to USD is legally fixed, eliminating domestic currency conversion risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Declaración Anual de la Sociedad) and payment of annual franchise tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the 31st of March each year or within 90 days of the anniversary of incorporation as prescribed by the tax code
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest of 1% per month or fraction thereof, surcharges up to 10%, and administrative suspension; continued non-compliance triggers fiscal interdiction and risk of strike-off by the Registro Público de Panamá.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Financial statements and independent auditor's report for companies meeting statutory asset or turnover thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI and, for regulated customs brokerage license holders, the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) supervision files
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 120 days following the end of the fiscal year, unless an extension is granted; normally March 31 for December year-end filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monetary fines for failure to file; revocation or suspension of customs brokerage license; director liability for false certifications.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Audit report on the annual sworn statement of assets and liabilities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due with the annual return under the general March 31 filing rule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty of 25% of the tax due, inflation-adjusted, plus interest; inability to obtain a solvency certificate.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: License renewal for customs brokerage house and customs agent registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual renewal by the licensee's anniversary date; generally filed during the last quarter of each calendar year for the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine and temporary suspension; failure to renew results in cancellation of the brokerage license and prohibition from customs operations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registry fee for commercial company registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the company's founding anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fees and suspension of registry filings; persistent non-payment leads to administrative strike-off of the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of economic substance for active licensed service companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI and ANA for customs operators
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after completion of the annual tax filing; generally by April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Rebuttable presumption of beneficial owner misdeclaration, tax penalties up to USD 10,000, and cancellation of the customs license for Sham substance failures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Companies with gross annual income exceeding USD 300,000 or total assets exceeding USD 500,000, or those required by the customs brokerage licensing authority to present audited financial statements, are subject to compulsory independent audit by a certified public accountant licensed in Panama.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by the Accounting Technical Committee of Panama (IFRS / full IFRS) for larger companies; small and medium-sized companies may choose IFRS for SMEs or the simplified local GAAP framework approved by the DGI for tax purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, each company must file a Confidential Registry of Final Beneficiaries with the DGI, confirming all transferred shares and changes in beneficial ownership. For customs brokerage license holders, an updated list of officers, directors, and ultimate beneficial owners must be submitted to the ANA. Transfers during the year must be reported no later than the subsequent annual confirmation, under penalty of fines and license suspension.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Shares and Transfer Ledger

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 1,200 per year for registered agent and registered office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - USD 7,500 for a certified independent audit of a small- to mid-sized customs brokerage entity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial sourcing rule; licensed customs brokers pay only on locally sourced gross fees. Deductible expenses include ACH customs bond fees, salaries, rent, and software; no statutory tax holiday exists for a Panama customs brokerage. Exclusively foreign-source fee streams (e.g., arranging clearance outside Panama) fall outside the 25% base, producing a potentially zero effective rate on those flows.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 111 (Declaración Anual de Renta de Personas Jurídicas); filed through the DGI e-Tax portal (Sistema de Retorno Electrónico) at dgi.mef.gob.pa
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; mandatory quarterly advance payments on Form 110 in April, June, September, and December for calendar-year taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; a Panamanian S.A. may adopt a non-calendar fiscal year. The deadline is the last business day of the third month following period close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross Panama-source revenues: all brokerage, clearing, forwarding, and bonded-carrier fees derived from customs procedures performed in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned S.A. must report only Panamanian-source revenue. Offshore revenue arising outside Panamanian territory is excluded and documented in the schedule of foreign-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: salaries of licensed customs brokers, rents, customs bond premiums, software, professional fees, and administrative costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate expenses between Panama-source and foreign-source revenue on a fair proportion; only expenses attributable to Panama operations are deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Special deductions: depreciation on fixed assets and amortization of goodwill or intangibles directly used in the licensed agency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Follow DGI depreciation tables; consider bonus depreciation election, and document legal title to the assets used by the Panama agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income and loss carryforward applied.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply confirmed NOL of prior 5 years only if the S.A. has timely filed prior Form 111 returns and audited financial statements under DGI requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax computed at 25%; advance payments and credits offset the assessed tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Credit quarterly advance payments made via Form 110; no foreign tax credit is available because only Panama-source income is taxed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration, signature, and date, including the Panamanian resident agent or legal representative signature block.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholder must execute a notarized power of attorney to an authorized resident agent; the agent signs under penalties of perjury.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is penalized by a surcharge of 10% of the ultimate tax deficiency for the first month, plus 1% per month thereafter up to a 50% cap, with default interest calculated and compounded daily from the original due date. Late quarterly Form 110 vouchers carry a fixed B/. 250 administrative penalty. Persistent non-filing may lead to a penalty equal to 2% to 10% of turnover and the temporary suspension of the customs broker license by the National Customs Authority.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% statutory WHT on cash and in-kind distributions of Panama-source profits to non-resident shareholders. Rate decreases to 5% when the distributing S.A. proves it has paid corporate income tax at the 25% full rate on the distributed profit pool.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama applies DTA relief on a territorial basis; non-resident shareholders must submit a TRC issued by the DGI or the tax authority of their residence, alongside a beneficial ownership declaration and supporting shares register extract, to the withholding agent before the dividend distribution. Files in support must be maintained for 5 years; DGI can refund excess WHT if the treaty rate is lower.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest paid by the S.A. to unrelated non-resident lenders for loans documented outside Panama is generally Panama-source-exempt. Royalties and fees paid for the use of trademarks, software, or know-how inside Panama attract a 15% WHT, reduced only under a DTA. Payments to connected offshore service companies are also exposed to 15% WHT plus TP adjustment.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 1,000,000 (Panama Balboa, pegged 1:1 to USD 1,000,000) in aggregate related-party transactions during the tax year. Above this threshold, a Form 733 sworn statement and a full Local File (and Master File where group turnover exceeds USD 50,000,000) must be filed.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Law 254 of 2021 ESR requires Panamanian entities deriving income from relevant activities abroad to prove economic substance. Custom clearance brokerage is not a named relevant activity, but the DGI and customs authority will nevertheless require physical office, dedicated staff, revenue commensurate with assets and risks, and board control in Panama for treaty and efiling claims; a pure letter-box customs broker is treated as a shell and is subject to ESR penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting a Form 111 that systematically underreports Panama-source clearance fees, or claiming fabricated deductible expenses and fictitious NOLs, with the deliberate intent to defraud the Fisco Nacional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty of triple the evaded tax (200% surcharge), plus default interest; in-court fiscal crime proceedings can impose imprisonment of 3 to 10 years. The corporate status of the S.A. may be cancelled by the Registro Público, and the preferential tax record revoked.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and registered legal representatives who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the tax deficiency, face civil restitution of evasion proceeds, travel bans restricting exit from Panama, and custodial sentences based on the amount defrauded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Private Interest Foundation (PIF) Misuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using an otherwise dormant PIF or nominee shareholder with no physical operations to hold the customs broker license, collect brokerage commissions, and shift profits out of Panama through bogus service invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Notification to the Unidad de Inteligencia Financiera (UIF) and seizure of bank accounts under Law 23 of 2015; fines up to PAB 1,000,000 for AML shortcomings and cancellation of the S.A.'s license to practice customs brokerage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors used to conceal beneficial ownership are treated as principals of a criminal violation, subject to administrative dissolution of the entity, personal fines of B/. 2,000 to B/. 50,000, 5-year travel bans, and imprisonment for up to 10 years for money structuring and money laundering.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Customs Fraud and False Brokerage Declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Filing false customs import/export declarations, underdeclaring ACH-processing freight values, misusing bonded transit regimes to move controlled goods, or releasing cargo without settlement of duties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas imposes administrative fines from 3% to 100% of the evaded duty and may suspend or permanently revoke the customs brokerage license (Registro de Agentes Aduaneros). Criminal smuggling carries imprisonment of 5 to 15 years and confiscation of cargo and warehouse.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director who signs or licenses the custom broker registration is personally liable for all compromised duty amounts, is subject to the immediate freezing of personal bank accounts, judicial travel bans, and the revocation of his or her individual customs brokering credentials.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing and Base Erosion Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payments of commissions or management fees to a related Panama PIF or foreign affiliate at inflated rates with no actual service, thin-capitalizing the S.A. using excessive shareholder debt to strip profits, or failing to file the Form 733 where related-party transactions exceed the threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI adjusts the taxable income upward, disallows the excessive deduction, and applies a deficiency penalty of 40% of the underpaid tax, plus monthly default interest. The taxpayer loses the preference to request advance pricing agreements and is barred from DTA relief until corrected.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who design artificial TP schemes are held jointly responsible for the tax adjustment and interest; they may be criminally indicted for misleading the DGI, face civil restitution for the hidden profit, and are subject to a travel ban pending the final ruling.
